messages:
jess (eng-oncall): paging alerts just fired for us-west-2 continuous-batcher pool, node g4-large-7 is thrashing, high RSS + swap in kernel. seeing CUDA OOMs and container crashes. paging spike -> latency > 3s for some customers.
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: continuous-batcher-high-memory at 2478901234 — severity P1 — notify: eng-oncall, eng-sre
jess (eng-oncall): stack traces in logs show 'CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED' followed by 'std::bad_alloc' in the batch scheduler. attaching tail.
jess (eng-oncall): ```
[2026-03-15T02:07:10Z] ERROR runtime: Kernel launch failed: CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_FAILED
[2026-03-15T02:07:11Z] WARN batching: batch growth detected, queue_len=4800, avg_latency=1800ms
[2026-03-15T02:07:12Z] ERROR prefetch: kv-cache prefill exceeded memory target (rss=27GB swap=3GB)
[2026-03-15T02:07:14Z] FATAL containerd: oom-kill process=continuous-batcher pid=42109
```
sam (eng-runtime): thanks, jess — are we seeing a single job with massive sequence length or steady growth from many small requests?
jess (eng-oncall): looks like steady growth after a config change 15m ago (kv prefetch factor bumped to 8 in canary), lots of medium-length requests. queue never drains.
olivia (eng-sre): my guess: prefetch + continuous batching = unbounded KV cache growth + larger effective batch sizes -> kernel memory blowout. need to back out the canary and drain node.
rahul (eng-infra): I can cordon/drain the node; suggest immediate drain to stop new pods scheduling, then scale down the daemon that sets prefetch.
michael (support): some customers reported 504s — support is triaging. can we get ETA on mitigation? need an incident summary for customers.
sam (eng-runtime): mitigation plan: 1) flip prefetch factor on canary to previous value (from 8 -> 2). 2) kill runaway batchers on node. 3) restart gpu driver if OOM persists. 4) monitor latency and 5xx rates.
jess (eng-oncall): rahul, can you drain? i’ll push the config rollback to canary only.
rahul (eng-infra): executing now: `kubectl cordon g4-large-7 && kubectl drain g4-large-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
rahul (eng-infra): node cordoned, eviction in progress (pods evicted=12).
jess (eng-oncall): rolling back canary config: `kubectl set env deploy/continuous-batcher PREFETCH_FACTOR=2 -n runtime-canary`
jess (eng-oncall): patched canary, restarting pods in that deployment.
sam (eng-runtime): also toggled `BATCH_MAX_WINDOW_MS` from 2000 -> 500 for canary to reduce accumulation.
olivia (eng-sre): good. while evictions finish, we should kill leftover long-lived processes on the node to free GPU memory: `crictl ps | grep continuous-batcher` then `crictl stop <pid>` if not draining cleanly.
rahul (eng-infra): did `crictl stop` on two stuck containers; logs show repeated 'kv-cache prefill loop' messages at 1000/s.
michael (support): seeing 504 count declining in the dashboard, customers note degraded perf but fewer failures. sending a short status note.
sam (eng-runtime): one container restarted but kernel still shows some swap pressure; if swap doesn't drop in 5m, we may have to reboot node.
jess (eng-oncall): monitoring telemetry: per-route p95 dropped from 2.8s -> 1.1s after the canary rollback and node drain. error rate from 1.7% -> 0.4%.
olivia (eng-sre): nice. create a short RCA pointer: immediate cause = aggressive kv prefetch factor combined with continuous batching recent change, leading to unbounded batch window and GPU memory overcommit -> OOM and container restarts.
sam (eng-runtime): follow-ups: add a guard in runtime to cap KV prefetch memory per-pod, add an autoslice to prevent unbounded batch accumulation, and add a preflight check for canary config changes that affect memory.
jess (eng-oncall): handoff: i'm wrapping up, handing to sam for post-incident follow-up. i'll post customer-facing blurb in #support-ops.
rahul (eng-infra): node g4-large-7 rebooted as a precaution, kernel memory and swap cleared. back to Ready.
michael (support): thanks — sending update to affected customers now, stating mitigation and ETA for RCA.
incident-bot: Incident resolved (2478901459) — status: mitigated, follow-up required.
sam (eng-runtime): filing a follow-up ticket linking logs, config diff, and suggested runtime safeguards. assigning to runtime and infra owners.
jess (eng-oncall): thanks team :thumbsup: — if anyone sees regressions re-alert here.
